newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar trapped in range, dull NY cited.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar trapped in range, dull NY cited.

text.p: White sugar futures were reluctant to push above opening levels as players opted to play the ranges after the recent repositioning of New York's structure after expiry, traders said on Tuesday.
The lacklustre performance on the raws market failed to inspire much activity in London after Monday's session saw unexpected volatility on both markets.
"It's just not moving around at all...it's a routine day's trading," said one trader.

Mixed trade and broker buying supported nearby London values at the lows but ranges remained tight. The day's turnover was boosted by a sprinkling of crosses and AA deals by commission house and trade players.
At 1700 GMT May was down 40 cents at $307.00 and August down 30 cents at $306.30. Volume was 1,013 lots.
May/August attracted limited interest and was said to have traded out to $1.10 but then narrowed to 60 cents.
Actual trades on the the May/May arbitrage were few, with the premium widening to a nominal $68, and sellers were reported to be waiting in the wings at around $70 to cap any gains.
Bangladesh provided about the only new physical news, although traders said Iran could soon be in the market again to buy white sugar.

The price said to have been paid by Bangladesh in its tender to buy a cargo of 150 ICUMSA March/April whites was $347.95 a tonne and the country is to tender again to buy a same-quality cargo on March 8 and 15.
Volume in Paris was relatively solid, with traders suggesting pre-hedging against Wednesday's European Union tender for export licences.
May was up 30 cents at $306.50 and August up $1.10 at $306.30. Matif volume amounted to 860 lots.
